newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portucel sees pulp sector recovery in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Portucel sees pulp sector recovery in 1997.

text.p: The pulp sector is set to recover in 1997, gradually in the first half before picking up pace in the second half, the president of Portuguese pulp producer Portucel Industrial Jorge Godinho said.
"In the first half of the year there will be a weak recovery, but in the second half the recovery will be more significant," Godinho told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He was speaking after the company announced a 1996 loss of 1.37 billion escudos, compared with a profit of 18.14 billion escudos in 1995.

Godinho said: "The recovery in 1997 will be built on the positive trend in global paper consumption, especially in Europe and the U.S., and the strong economic activity in various parts of the world, particularly Asia and the U.S."
He added: "As 1996 was a bad year for the pulp sector, many investment decisions were postponed, and so some over-capacity and over-stocking from 1996 will be absorbed in 1997."
Godinho said prices of white eucalyptus pulp had remained steady in early 1997 at the levels of end-1996 -- around 400 Ecus per tonne.
